subject: general
question: A dentist usually uses:
solution:
The correct answer is __**a concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A dentist uses a concave mirror to examine the teeth.
 
• Concave mirrors provide a magnified and upright image of the teeth, which helps in detailed examination.
 
• The curved surface of a concave mirror helps in focusing light, providing better illumination in the oral cavity.
 
• Concave mirrors are preferred because they allow dentists to see a larger area of the mouth clearly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror:**

 
 
• A convex mirror diverges light rays and is used for a wider field of view, such as in vehicle side mirrors.
 
• It provides a smaller, upright, and diminished image, which is not suitable for dental examination.
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirror:**
 
 
• A plane mirror reflects light without altering the size of the image.
 
• It provides a virtual, upright image of the same size as the object, but it does not magnify, making it less useful for detailed dental work.
 
 
 
• **Plano-Convex Mirror:**
 
 
• A plano-convex mirror is typically used in focusing applications, such as in telescopes and laser systems.
 
• It is not used in dental practices due to its specific focusing properties.
 
 
 
• **Optical Properties:**
 
 
• Concave mirrors converge light rays to a focal point, allowing for magnification of the image.
 
• Convex mirrors and plane mirrors do not offer the same level of magnification and focus required for dental examinations.
